target: pedicel length ca. 4 cm (flowering); pedicel length up to 9.5 cm present_during PO_0001002
fix: Pattern 'X ca. a, to b at fruiting' gives two values for two stages: the first number is the flowering size and only the 'to b' is scoped by 'at fruiting'. Do not merge them into one range a–b under the fruiting stage.
reason: The flora gives about 4 cm for the pedicel in general (at flowering) and up to 9.5 cm only in fruit. A range of 4–9.5 cm at fruiting is not what the flora says.
The habit of the whole plant is given as prostrate, ascending or erect, and these are the three alternatives recorded.
'2-flowered at each node' on the raceme rachis means 2 flowers per node. The count and the per-node position are right.
The inflorescence is 'many flowered', so flowers are present with a count of many, inside the inflorescence.
The frond lamina varies from pinnatifid to unequally lobed, which is a range of shapes. Both value terms fit the words.

target: cauline leaf lamina, proximal cauline leaves
fix: In 'basal blade X, cauline Y proximally, becoming Z distally', the words 'cauline' and 'proximally' restrict the shape to the lower stem leaves. The whole/position slot must carry the cauline leaf and the proximal position.
reason: The flora says basal blades are spatulate and distal cauline blades are lanceolate. Without the context, 'leaf lamina obovate, oblanceolate or spatulate' is false for the distal leaves.

fix: 'Fruit n-lobed' counts lobes of the fruit, not leaf lamina lobes. A lobe word should take its whole from the noun of the statement (here the fruit), not default to the leaf lamina lobe.
reason: The statement is about the fruit, which has 1–3 lobes with one seed in each. No leaf is involved.
The disc floret corollas range from yellow to orange-yellow. This is a colour continuum on the corolla.
'Flaccid' (limp, drooping) young leaves are best covered by the existing term flexible, and the 'young' context is kept.
Spatulate is one end of the stated range 'rhomboid to spatulate' for the petals of female flowers, so the statement is true.

target: leaf venation: vascular bundle (PO_0005020) in leaf, pinnate (PATO_0000410)
fix: 'nervation pennée' / 'pinnately veined' describes the leaf venation. Putting 'pinnate' on the leaf itself would mean a pinnately compound leaf.
reason: The leaves of Kleinia fulgens are simple. It is the venation that is pinnate, with weak lateral veins.
'Yellowish' is read as approximately yellow. The seed colour is right.
9–14 secondary veins on each side of the midvein. The bearer, count and landmark are right.

fix: A shape given after 'Cauline leaves ...; sessile; blade ...' belongs to the cauline leaves. The whole slot must keep 'cauline' when basal leaves are described separately.
reason: The continuum from oblong to ovate is right, but it is said only of the cauline leaf blades. As a statement about all leaf laminas it misstates the basal leaves.
The leaf blade margin is serrate, and serrated on the leaf lamina is right.
The petal apex is mucronate, and the scope was correctly moved from the petal to the petal apex.
The blades are minutely pubescent on the upper surface, which is the adaxial side of the leaf lamina.
'Stamens many' means stamens are present with a count of many.
Anthers 'with filiform trichomes' means the anthers are hairy.

fix: 'secondary veins n on each side of midvein' should map to secondary leaf vein (as in A03042), not to the generic vascular bundle that 'vein' maps to. 'secondary veins' is a multi-word label and should win over the single word 'vein'.
reason: The count is of secondary veins of the leaflet blades, not of vascular bundles in general.

fix: 'Angled' said of fruits, stems or seeds means having angles or ridges in cross-section (angular). It does not mean bent, even though PATO lists 'angled' as a synonym of bent. The synonym 'angled' → bent should be blocked for organ cross-sections.
reason: The Carya fruit is described as not compressed and not angled, which is about its cross-section, not about being bent.
15–30 bracts (involucral) are counted on the head.
'Baccate' means berry-like, that is fleshy, and the context also says 'fleshy, succulent'.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) on leaf (and stem), color white
fix: In 'X with ... white hairs', the colour belongs to the hairs, not to X. Adjectives inside a 'with <noun>' phrase describe that noun.
reason: The hairs are white. The leaves are not said to be white.

target: lower petal shape rhomboid (PATO_0001938) AND petal apex acute (FLOPO_0991095)
fix: A hyphenated shape plus apex word (rhombic-acute, ovate-acuminate, oblong-obtuse) is two qualities joined: the outline shape and the apex shape. It is not a continuum between them.
reason: 'Rhombic' and 'acute' are not points on one scale. Here the lower petal is rhombic with an acute tip.
The lobe apex is usually acute to acuminate. Sharpness on the leaf lamina lobe gives the meaning, though the lobe apex would be a finer bearer.

fix: 'Branches' in a sentence that starts with 'Panicle ...' are inflorescence branches, not shoot branches (PO_0025073). The container noun should fix the reading of 'branches'.
reason: These are the panicle branches, 2 per node, of the grass. The ascending-to-spreading range with 'at maturity' is otherwise acceptable.
3 or 4 lateral veins on each side of the midrib. The bearer, count and landmark are right.
In 'leaf blade 2–4 × 1.2–2 cm' the first figures are the length, 2–4 cm.
The staminate flowers are in axillary umbels, so an umbel inflorescence is present.
